boundary_notes: Edge cases vs other skills: pure data modeling fixes that improve IQ accuracy → also data-integration; per-tenant IQ token scoping → also multitenancy; styling IQ components → theming; IQ in React Native (NOT supported); IQ returns wrong answers → troubleshooting FIRST; hosted MCP server setup, embed MCP sessions, and agentId MCP URLs -> mcp; new chart types for AI to use -> custom-charts.

evals.prompt: I want to add an AI chat widget to our embedded analytics so users can ask questions about their data in plain English. We're using React. How do I embed the IQ Chat component and wire it up securely?
evals.expected_output: A docs-first answer that: covers the LuzmoIQChatComponent for React, explains that the embed token must be generated server-side and only authKey/authToken passed to the frontend, and mentions the IQ add-on license requirement.
expectations: Mentions `LuzmoIQChatComponent` for React
States that IQ is available as an add-on license
Explains that the embed token is generated server-side
States that only `authKey` and `authToken` are passed to the frontend
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/iq--introduction--chat-component.md`

evals.prompt: I want to send a question to Luzmo IQ from our Node.js backend and display the answer in our own custom UI — not the built-in chat widget. Which API do I use and what does the request look like?
evals.expected_output: Direct the user to the /aiprompt API (POST /0.1.0/aiprompt) for server-side prompts. Should consult https://developer.luzmo.com/api/createAIPrompt.md before describing the request shape.
expectations: Identifies `/aiprompt` or `createAIPrompt` as the correct API (not legacy IQMessage)
States that this is a backend / server-side API call
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/api/createAIPrompt.md`
Does not invent request/response shapes without fetching the docs

evals.prompt: What's the difference between the IQ Chat component and the IQ Answer component? My designer wants to show the answer to a specific question inline in our dashboard page, not a full conversational widget.
evals.expected_output: Clear explanation: IQ Chat is a full conversational UI; IQ Answer renders a specific analytics answer without the chat UI. For a non-chat inline answer, the Answer component is appropriate.
expectations: Explains that IQ Chat is a full conversational widget
Explains that IQ Answer renders a specific answer inline without the full chat UI
Recommends the Answer component for the described use case
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/iq--introduction--answer-component.md`

evals.prompt: We're building an LLM-powered agent using Claude that needs to answer data questions about our Luzmo datasets. How can the agent call Luzmo IQ as a tool?
evals.expected_output: Guide the user to the Luzmo IQ agentic workflow docs and/or hosted MCP, covering /aiprompt or MCP answer_question as a tool for function calling in an LLM agent loop.
expectations: References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/guides--adding-luzmo-iq-to-agentic-workflow.md` and/or `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/mcp--introduction.md`
Mentions `/aiprompt` or MCP tools (`answer_question`, `create_chart`) as agent-callable analytics interfaces
Explains the agentic pattern: agent calls Luzmo when a data question is detected

evals.prompt: Can I use the Luzmo IQ chat component in a React Native mobile app? We're building a native iOS/Android app and want the conversational AI widget in it.
evals.expected_output: A clear statement that React Native is not supported for the IQ Chat and Answer components, without fabricating a workaround.
expectations: Clearly states that React Native is not supported for IQ Chat and Answer components
Does not suggest a React Native workaround that is not documented
Optionally suggests using a web view as a potential approach or contacting support

evals.prompt: Our Luzmo IQ keeps returning wrong answers - it picks the wrong datasets and doesn't understand our column names. We have 45 datasets in the token scope. How do I improve IQ answer quality?
evals.expected_output: Identifies token scope as too broad (45 datasets), recommends narrowing to 5-10 relevant datasets, and emphasizes dataset/column naming, descriptions, and subtypes for quality.
expectations: Identifies over-broad token scope (45 datasets) as a primary issue
Recommends narrowing `access.datasets` in the embed token to 5-10 relevant datasets
Mentions dataset and column naming best practices
Suggests adding column descriptions for calculated fields
References column subtypes (currency, duration) for proper formatting
May reference the IQ quality fundamentals section or data modeling patterns

evals.prompt: We're embedding IQ Chat for our SaaS customers. Each customer should only be able to ask questions about their own data — not see other customers' rows when IQ queries the datasets. How do I set this up?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a multi-tenant data isolation requirement for IQ. The skill should route to multitenancy for the isolation implementation (parameter_overrides / EmbedFilterGroup), while noting the IQ-specific consideration of scoping access.datasets to the tenant's datasets.
expectations: Recognizes this is a multi-tenant isolation problem, not just an IQ quality problem
Routes to `multitenancy` for the data isolation implementation
Mentions that the embed token's `access.datasets` must be scoped to only the tenant's datasets
Notes that `parameter_overrides` (Pattern 1) ensures IQ cannot see other tenants' rows even when it picks the right dataset
Does NOT present only narrowing dataset scope as sufficient — row-level isolation also requires multitenancy patterns

evals.prompt: We created a Luzmo Agent called Revenue assistant and I want our Node backend to call it. I was going to POST /aiprompt with agent: 'analyst', task: 'generate', and agent_id set to the Agent's id. Is that the right request?
evals.expected_output: Sending agent and agent_id together is valid: agent: 'analyst' runs the analyst with the saved Agent's datasets and published Rules, but the Agent's capabilities are not used. Omit agent (or send 'auto') to run the universal agent with the Agent's capabilities. Call /aiprompt with the user's embed token, not the organization API key. Point at the Agents guide and createAIPrompt docs.
expectations: Uses `agent_id` for the saved Agent
States that `agent_id` may be combined with `agent` (for example `analyst`), and that the Agent's datasets and published Rules then apply
States that with `agent` set the saved Agent's capabilities are not used; omitting `agent` (or `auto`) runs the universal agent with those capabilities
Identifies `/aiprompt` or `createAIPrompt` as the invocation API
States that the call uses the user's embed token
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/guides--creating-and-using-agents-through-the-api.md` or `https://developer.luzmo.com/api/createAIPrompt.md`

evals.prompt: I linked a discount-policy Rule to our Agent, then edited the text through the API. The Agent still answers with the old policy. The Rule response shows has_unpublished_changes: true. What did I miss?
evals.expected_output: Saving a Rule appends a version and does not change what Agents run. Publish the new version. A draft-only Rule contributes nothing even while linked.
expectations: States that a linked Rule applies only its currently published version
States that saving or updating appends a version and does not change Agent behavior until that version is published
Explains that `has_unpublished_changes: true` means a newer version exists than the published one
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/guides--creating-and-managing-rules-through-the-api.md` or the saved-agents guidance

evals.prompt: IQ keeps treating refunds as positive revenue. The column is named Revenue and the description says 'order revenue'. Refunds are stored as negative amounts, and revenue should be net of refunds. Where do I record that so IQ uses it?
evals.expected_output: Keep the name and description. Put the definition and sign convention in ai_context on the column or dataset. ai_context is plain text, not a localized object. Do not rely on description alone.
expectations: Identifies `ai_context` as the field for the refund / net-revenue definition
States that `ai_context` is plain text and not a localized name/description object
States that name and description stay; AI context enriches them
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/guide/guides--managing-ai-context.md` or the data-modeling-for-iq guidance

evals.prompt: One prompt from our users can ask for an answer, a chart, and a full dashboard at once. Which /aiprompt agent handles that, and how do I limit it to analysis and charts only?
evals.expected_output: Use the universal agent: agent 'auto' (task generate) with capabilities ['data_analysis','chart_creation']. Omitting capabilities enables every capability the user may use. Requires the IQ addon.
expectations: Recommends `agent: 'auto'` (the universal agent)
Shows `capabilities` with `data_analysis` and `chart_creation` to exclude dashboard creation
States that omitting `capabilities` enables every capability available to the user
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/api/createAIPrompt.md`

evals.prompt: We embed LuzmoIQChatComponent in React. We created a 'Finance assistant' Agent with two datasets and a published Rule. How do we make the embedded chat use that Agent?
evals.expected_output: Set the agentId prop on LuzmoIQChatComponent (react-embed 7.3.0+). The chat runs the analyst with the Agent's datasets and published Rules. The embed token must still grant use on those datasets.
expectations: Uses the `agentId` prop on `LuzmoIQChatComponent`
Mentions a minimum package version (`@luzmo/react-embed` 7.3.0 or later)
States that the embed token must still grant `use` on the Agent's datasets
Does not claim the IQ Answer component supports `agentId`

evals.prompt: Our PM wants a weekly report of questions our embedded users asked IQ that failed or were out of scope, per customer. Is there an API for that?
evals.expected_output: Yes: the read-only ailog resource (search / detail / conversation), filtered by success, out_of_scope, source 'embedded', and suborganization_id. Owner/admin only, plan-gated, 30-day retention. Also the Agent Logs page.
expectations: Identifies the `ailog` API (Search AILog) or the Agent Logs page
Mentions filters such as `success`, `out_of_scope`, `source`, or `suborganization_id`
States that only owners and admins can read AI logs and that retention is 30 days
References `https://developer.luzmo.com/api/searchAILog.md`

evals.prompt: We already embed a Luzmo dashboard with the web component. Can our users ask IQ questions about that dashboard without us building a chat UI?
evals.expected_output: Yes: enable Luzmo IQ in the dashboard settings in Studio. The embedded dashboard shows a dashboard-aware IQ panel that respects active filters and inherits theme and language. Token scoping still applies.
expectations: States that IQ can be enabled from the dashboard settings in Luzmo Studio without code changes
Mentions that the panel is dashboard-aware (respects dashboard filters)
Keeps the embed token scoping requirement
References `https://academy.luzmo.com/article/fyeoiaei` or the Path G guidance
